s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The subcutaneous node was first noticed 10 years ago
The node has been slowly growing
The patient experienced swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
The swelling disappeared with lactation
The patient experienced mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
A solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque is present in the right axilla
The plaque measures 5 × 3 cm
Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells are diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern'
Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Imaging studies show no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

shortlist.label: breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: positive for estrogen receptor and GATA3 antibodies, and presence of apocrine glands

shortlist.label: accessory axillary breast tissue
shortlist.why_kept: presence of apocrine glands and estrogen receptor positivity

shortlist.label: epithelioid sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: histopathology showing dermal tumor infiltrating subcutaneous fat with Indian file pattern

shortlist.label: adenosquamous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: immunohistochemistry positive for pancytokeratin and cytokeratin 20

shortlist.label: fibroadenoma in ectopic breast tissue
shortlist.why_kept: presence of apocrine glands and estrogen receptor positivity, and benign clinical course

raw.rationale: The patient's history of swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy and menstrual cycles, along with the presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands, suggests a strong hormonal influence on the tumor, which is consistent with accessory breast tissue. The 'Indian file pattern' of tumor cells and the positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: breast cancer
rejected.why: While the immunohistochemistry profile is consistent with breast cancer, the lack of a primary tumor in the breast and the presence of apocrine glands in the axilla suggest that this is not a metastatic breast cancer.

rejected.label: epithelioid sarcoma
rejected.why: The tumor's morphology and immunohistochemistry profile do not match those of epithelioid sarcoma, which typically shows a more aggressive growth pattern and lacks the strong hormonal influence seen in this case.

rejected.label: adenosquamous carcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's morphology and immunohistochemistry profile do not match those of adenosquamous carcinoma, which typically shows a more complex growth pattern with both glandular and squamous components.

rejected.label: fibroadenoma in ectopic breast tissue
rejected.why: While fibroadenoma is a possible diagnosis in ectopic breast tissue, the presence of atypical epithelioid tumor cells and the 'Indian file pattern' of infiltration suggest a more complex lesion than a typical fibroadenoma.
